title: Split constraints.py module into constraints/ package
body:
**When merged this MR will:**
- Split `ase/constraints.py` into separate files `ase/constraints/*.py` (Separate commit for each extraction)
- Enable and apply ruff formatting to constraints
- Close #1887

# Checklist: `x` (done) or `~` (irrelevant)

- [x] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://ase-lib.org/development/contribute.html)
- [~] [**Doc strings** in code changed in this MR are up to date.](https://ase-lib.org/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code)
- [~] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://ase-lib.org/development/tests.html)
- [~] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://ase-lib.org/development/writing_changelog.html)
- [~] [**Issue is resolved** via "closes #XXXX" if applicable.](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/issues/managing_issues.html#closing-issues-automatically)
author: SebastianWellig

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
This seems a very welcome tidy-up! And a good chance to get more of the code `ruff format`-ed at the same time? It might take a bit of time to review as we'll want to take a quick look through and make sure nothing odd crept in.

I am labelling this "response-needed" as a prompt to discuss it in the next maintainers catch-up.

comments.author: SebastianWellig
comments.body:
> And a good chance to get more of the code `ruff format`-ed at the same time?

Considering the MR is already gigantic as it is, maybe it would be better to revert formatting and disable it for now, so that it could be addressed in a dedicated MR for ruff formatting.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests applying `ruff format` to more of the code as part of this PR, which implies a concrete code change.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @SebastianWellig for the nice clean-up!

I have compared each new file with the original `constraints.py` using IDE (VS code "Compare" functionality) and found no substantial changes except Ruff formatting, so it looks all OK to me.

The only thing I like to suggest is about the file name.
Both [PEP8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/#package-and-module-names) and [the Google style guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html#3164-guidelines-derived-from-guidos-recommendations) suggest using underscores for files to connect words (although some ASE files do not very much follow them).
Following this, I would suggest e.g.:

- `fixatoms.py` -> `fix_atoms.py`
- `fixedline.py` -> `fixed_line.py`
- `mirrorforce.py` -> `mirror_force.py`
- `externalforce.py` -> `external_force.py`

These will improve readability, and the files `fix_XXX.py` and `fixed_YYY.py` are well grouped.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Explicitly suggests renaming several files to use underscores per PEP8 and Google style guide conventions (e.g., fixatoms.py -> fix_atoms.py).

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Unrelated: @ajjackson @yuzie007 When we label something as ~"response-needed", whose response are we requesting?  I suggest renaming the label because even if I know the answer, not all contributors would.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: Indeed, I am using it to mean "flag for discussion in maintainer meeting and decide response there". I think the label may have existed before the regular TSC meetings did, and we adopted it? How about we start using something like "awaiting maintainers discussion" or "maintainer-meeting-needed"?

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
I was also a bit wondering "who should *respond* to whom". Renaming the label should clarify this.

Something like "awaiting maintainers discussion" sounds a good idea. With this we can beforehand mark issues and MRs that require discussion/agreement.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: what about `maint-discuss`, it's kind of short and it looks like it belongs to maintainers

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests renaming the 'response-needed' label to something clearer, which is an actionable improvement to the project's process/tooling.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Generally very nice to do this, thanks a lot!

thread.actionability_reasoning: Pure acknowledgment and praise with no code change implied.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: Sounds like we have three maintainers onboard in principle, and of those Yuji has checked the files. We can go ahead if @yuzie007 is happy?

thread.actionability_reasoning: Meta-discussion about merge readiness and review logistics, no code change implied.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: OK, let's go merging! Thank you very much @SebastianWellig for the very careful migration!

thread.actionability_reasoning: Pure acknowledgment and merge approval, no code change implied.
